summary: Henry Thoby Prinsep was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Tonbridge School (~1805–1807) and the East India Company College (1807–1808), and later served in the Indian Civil Service (~1809–1843).

Henry Thomas Colebrooke was an Indologist who studied under Citrapati (~1794–1800). His career included serving in the East India Company (~1782–1814), holding a professorship at Fort William College (1782–1814), and directing the Royal Asiatic Society (~1823–1837).

Henry Thomas Francis worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Cambridge (B.A. 1856–1860) under Edward Byles Cowell, later becoming a Fellow at Gonville and Caius College (1861–1873) and Under-Librarian at Cambridge University Library (1877).
Henry Thomas Rogers, who worked in Indology and Buddhist studies, studied at Addiscombe Military Seminary (1848–1849). He later served as Principal of the College of Engineering, Guindy (~1869–1880).
Henry White Wallis was an Indologist who studied at the University of Cambridge under Edward Byles Cowell in 1882. He later served as a Fellow at Gonville and Caius College (~1886–1887).

Henry Whitehead studied at Eton College, the University of Oxford, Balliol College, and Princeton University. He held posts at Buckmaster & Moore (1927–1928), Balliol College (1932–1941), the UK Government (1941–1945), and the University of Oxford (1945–1960).
Henry Whitelock Torrens was an Indologist who studied at Christ Church, Oxford (B.A. 1823–1825/1826). He later served as Secretary of The Asiatic Society from 1840 to 1846.
Henry William Byerley Thomson studied at University College London and Jesus College, Cambridge (B.A. ~1840–1846). He later served as Queen’s Advocate of Ceylon (1858) and Puisne Judge (1861–1867).

Henry Yule was a scholar of history, archaeology, Indology, and linguistics. He studied at University College London and Addiscombe Military Seminar, later serving on the Council of India (1875–1889) and presiding over the Hakluyt Society and Royal Asiatic Society.
Heramba Chandra Chackravarty was an Indologist who studied under Manindra Mohan Bose. He served as a Lecturer at City College, Kolkata (attested 1977).

Herbert Arthur Popley worked in Indology and religious studies after earning a B.A. at Hackney College. He served as a missionary with the London Missionary Society (1901), founded the Community Training School, Erode, and worked with the YMCA (1921).

Herbert Cushing Tolman worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Indology, and linguistics, earning his Ph.D. at Yale under William Dwight Whitney. He taught at Wisconsin and North Carolina before serving at Vanderbilt University (1894–1923), including as Dean.

Herbert Fletcher De Cou was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the University of Michigan and the American School of Classical Studies at Athens, later teaching Greek and Sanskrit at Michigan (1892–1893).

Herbert Franke studied Sinology and Central Asian studies under Erich Haenisch and Erich Hauer, completing degrees at Cologne, Bonn, and Berlin. He was a professor at the University of Munich (1952–1979) and president of the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities.
Herbert Frederick Samman, an Indologist and linguist, studied at Emmanuel College (~1890–1893). He later served as Lecturer in Bengali at the University of Cambridge from 1922 to 1935.

Herbert Galton, a scholar of linguistics and Indology, studied at the University of Vienna in 1935 under Nikolai Trubetzkoy and Wilhelm Geiger. He later served as Professor of Slavic Linguistics at the University of Kansas (1962–1988).

Herbert Hope Risley worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. Educated at Winchester College and New College, Oxford, he later served as Permanent Secretary of the Judicial Department at the India Office in 1910.

Herbert Härtel specialized in Indology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies, earning his doctorate at Göttingen under Ernst Waldschmidt. He served as Director of the Museum of Asian Art (1963–1986) and held an honorary professorship at the Free University of Berlin.

Herbert Karl Alfred Plaeschke was an Indologist and historian who completed his degrees and habilitation at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg under Heinz Mode and Karl Ammer. He worked as a researcher at the University and State Library of Saxony-Anhalt (~1959–1993).

Herbert Leonard Offley Garrett, a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology, studied at St John's College (~1899–1902). He taught at Queen's College (1904–1912) and served as Vice-Principal (1919) and Principal (1927–1936) at Government College University, Lahore.
